newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbekistan to have fully private banks - decree.
newsitem.headline: Uzbekistan to have fully private banks - decree.

text.p: Uzbekistan, seeking to establish a system of fully private banks, allowed its citizens on Friday to set up banks.
Uzbek President Islam Karimov said in a decree the share of individuals in the capital of private banks must not be less than 50 percent.
The decree, published in official newspapers, says individuals wishing to found a bank will not have to declare the source of their earnings.
"Ungrounded interference of controlling bodies in the activity of private banks is not allowed," the decree said.
Uzbekistan's law on the banking system adopted last year provided for the existence of commercial banks set up by companies but said nothing about individuals.
The Central Bank will now have to bring its documents and activity in line with the present decree within one week.
Karimov also said private banks will be exempt from taxes on revenues for three years, with the money to be invested to improve infrastructure and technical means.
The decree set minimal capital of private banks at an equivalent of 250,000 Ecus and said it should remain unchanged for the first three years.

The Central Bank earlier sent a letter to other commercial banks ordering them to raise their capital to an equivalent of two million Ecus if based in Tashkent and one million Ecus if they are located outside the capital.
